## Where the work is

- **Just landed.** One spelling for reverse topology, [issue #262](https://github.com/chahyasantoso/motion5/issues/262). The internal field was `GraphIR.dependents` and the public query has always been `dependantsOf`: two spellings of one word, one letter apart, in one codebase, which is what makes two things look like they might be different concepts when they are not. The internal spelling moves to the public one rather than the other way around, and the reason is ownership rather than taste: `dependantsOf` on `ProjectHandle` is the only half with callers outside this package, because `index.ts` keeps graph internals private, so renaming it would break a contract to tidy one that nobody can see, and every ADR, guide, evidence-case file name and paragraph of prose in this tree already says dependant. So `deriveDependents` is `deriveDependants`, `GraphIR.dependents` is `GraphIR.dependants`, `PublisherSnapshot` inherits the renamed field, and the reverse-topology locals in `graph/order.ts` follow, singular included. No behaviour moves, no test is added, and nothing is deleted: `typecheck` is what a rename is proved by rather than a case that could only assert the suite is still green, every identifier is the same length so the formatter sees no reflow and no file changes size, and the existing suite is the regression. `packages/core/test/unit/graph/graph-dependents.test.ts` becomes `graph-dependants.test.ts` with `RA-18` through `RA-22` unchanged inside it, and the citation above moves with it. Archived documents under `docs/archived/` keep the spelling they shipped with.
- **Landed after that closure, and it is debt rather than a slice.**
